words.ex: She wore a white veil on her wedding day.
words.ex_cn: 她在婚礼那天戴了一条白色的面纱。
words.en: A veil is a piece of thin soft cloth that women sometimes wear over their heads and which can also cover their face.

words.ex: The car stopped at the verge of the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车停在了道路的边缘。
words.en: The edge or border of something; to be close to a certain state or condition.

words.ex: The fishing vessel sailed out at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 那艘渔船在黎明时出海。
words.en: A vessel is a large boat or a container for holding liquids.

words.ex: The park is in the vicinity of my house.
words.ex_cn: 公园在我家附近。
words.en: The area or region near or about a place; the surrounding district.

words.ex: He put vinegar on his salad.
words.ex_cn: 他把醋倒在沙拉上。
words.en: A sour-tasting liquid used as a condiment or preservative, typically made by fermenting dilute alcoholic liquids such as wine, cider, or beer.

words.ex: The evidence warrants a new investigation.
words.ex_cn: 证据使新的调查成为必要。
words.en: If something warrants a particular action, it makes the action seem necessary or appropriate for the circumstances.

words.ex: It is wasteful to leave the lights on all day.
words.ex_cn: 整天开着灯是浪费的。
words.en: If you describe something as wasteful, you disapprove of it because it uses too much of something valuable, such as time, money, or energy.

words.ex: This jacket is waterproof.
words.ex_cn: 这件夹克是防水的。
words.en: Something that is waterproof does not let water pass through it.

words.ex: Farmers grow wheat in the field.
words.ex_cn: 农民在田里种植小麦。
words.en: Wheat is a cereal plant that is grown in temperate countries and is the most important kind grown for food.

words.tr:
n. 鞭子
v. 鞭打；抽打；突然移动
words.ex: The farmer used a whip to guide the horse.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用鞭子赶马。
words.en: To whip means to hit a person or animal with a whip, or to move something quickly and suddenly.

words.ex: The width of the table is one meter.
words.ex_cn: 桌子的宽度是一米。
words.en: The width of something is the distance it measures from one side to the other.

words.tr:
n. 枯萎；凋谢；憔悴；
v. 枯萎；凋谢；憔悴；
words.ex: The flowers showed signs of wilt after the long heat.
words.ex_cn: 这些花在长时间高温后出现了枯萎的迹象。
words.en: If a plant wilts, it bends over because it is too dry, too hot, or too weak to stay upright.

words.tr:
adj. 值得的；有…价值；
n. 价值；
words.ex: This book is worth reading.
words.ex_cn: 这本书值得读。
words.en: If something is worth a particular amount of money, it can be sold for that amount or is considered to have that value.

words.ex: It is worthwhile to learn a new language.
words.ex_cn: 学习一门新语言是值得的。
words.en: If something is worthwhile, it is enjoyable or useful enough to make the effort or money spent on it seem reasonable.

words.tr: adj. 值得…的；值得尊敬的；
words.ex: This book is worthy of reading.
words.ex_cn: 这本书值得读。
words.en: If something or someone is worthy of something, they deserve it because they have the qualities or abilities required.

words.ex: He bought a new accessory for his phone.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的手机买了一个新配件。
words.en: An accessory is something such as a bag or piece of jewelry that you wear or carry because it is attractive.

words.ex: He was late, so he left accordingly.
words.ex_cn: 他迟到了，于是相应地提前出发了。
words.en: In a way that is appropriate to the particular circumstances.

words.tr: adj. 敏锐的；急性的；严重的；
words.ex: He has an acute mind and solves problems quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他思维敏锐，能快速解决问题。
words.en: An acute problem or negative feeling is very severe.

words.ex: He finished the work ahead of time.
words.ex_cn: 他提前完成了工作。
words.en: If someone is ahead in a competition or comparison, they are winning or doing better than the other people involved.

words.tr:
n. 业余爱好者；
adj. 业余的；
words.ex: He is an amateur who paints on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 他是个周末画画的业余爱好者。
words.en: An amateur is someone who does something as a hobby and not as a job.

words.tr: adj. 模棱两可的；含糊不清的；
words.ex: His answer was ambiguous and confused everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答模棱两可，让所有人都感到困惑。
words.en: If you describe something as ambiguous, you mean that it is unclear or confusing because it can be understood in more than one way.

words.ex: This rule is applicable to all students.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则适用于所有学生。
words.en: If something is applicable to a particular situation, it is relevant or suitable for that situation.

words.ex: The flowers in the garden are artificial.
words.ex_cn: 花园里的花是人造的。
words.en: Made or produced by human beings rather than occurring naturally, especially as a copy of something natural.

words.ex: The balloon will ascend into the sky.
words.ex_cn: 气球将升上天空。
words.en: If you ascend a hill or staircase, you go up it. If a staircase or path ascends, it leads up to a higher place.

words.tr:
v. 把…归因于；由…引起；
n. 品质；属性；特征；属性；
words.ex: He attributes his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you attribute something to an event or situation, you think that it was caused by that event or situation.

words.tr: adj. 真正的；真实的；真迹的；可靠的；
words.ex: This is an authentic painting by Picasso.
words.ex_cn: 这是一幅毕加索的真迹。
words.en: If something is authentic, it is real, true, or what people say it is.

words.tr:
adj. 辅助的；附属的
n. 辅助物；附属物；助动词
words.ex: He used an auxiliary verb to form the past tense.
words.ex_cn: 他使用了一个助动词来构成过去时。
words.en: An auxiliary is a person or thing that provides additional help or support.

words.ex: He barely slept last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚几乎没睡觉。
words.en: You use barely to say that something is only just true or only just the case.

words.ex: The barren land cannot grow any crops.
words.ex_cn: 这片贫瘠的土地无法种植任何庄稼。
words.en: If you describe something as barren, you mean that it is not able to produce anything, especially plants or crops.

words.tr:
v. 有益于；有助于；
n. 利益；好处；
words.ex: Exercise benefits your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼有益于你的健康。
words.en: A benefit is something that helps you or improves your life in some way.

words.ex: The coffee had a strong bitterness.
words.ex_cn: 这杯咖啡有很重的苦味。
words.en: Bitterness is the quality of having a sharp, pungent taste or of feeling angry and unhappy because of bad experiences.

words.ex: The glass is brittle and breaks easily.
words.ex_cn: 这种玻璃很硬但容易碎。
words.en: If something is brittle, it is hard and easily broken.

words.tr: v. 擦伤；挫伤；出现伤痕；
words.ex: He bruised his knee when he fell off the bike.
words.ex_cn: 他从自行车上摔下来时擦伤了膝盖。
words.en: A bruise is a mark that appears on your skin after you have been injured, but the skin is not broken.

words.tr:
n. 捆；束；包
v. 匆匆送走
words.ex: He bought a bundle of newspapers.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一捆报纸。
words.en: A bundle is a number of things that are tied or wrapped together so that they can be carried or stored easily.

words.ex: He has the capacity to solve hard math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他有能力解决复杂的数学问题。
words.en: The capacity of a place or container is the amount of things or people that it can hold.

words.tr: adj. 随意的；非正式的；偶然的；
words.ex: He wore casual clothes to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了随意的衣服去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone's attitude or behavior as casual, you mean they are not very concerned about what they are doing or what is happening around them, or they are not taking it seriously.

words.ex: The water freezes at zero centigrade.
words.ex_cn: 水在零摄氏度时结冰。
words.en: Centigrade is a scale for measuring temperature, in which water freezes at 0 degrees and boils at 100 degrees.

words.ex: The pencil is 15 centimetres long.
words.ex_cn: 这支铅笔长15厘米。
words.en: A centimetre is a unit of length in the metric system equal to one hundredth of a metre.

words.ex: There is no certainty that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天是否会下雨还没有确定。
words.en: Something that is certain is sure to happen or is definitely true.

words.tr:
n. 特点；特性；
adj. 典型的；特有的；
words.ex: Honesty is a key characteristic of a good friend.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是一个好朋友的关键特点。
words.en: A characteristic is a quality or feature that is typical of someone or something.

words.tr: v. 描述…的特性；以…为特征；
words.ex: This book characterizes the hero as brave and kind.
words.ex_cn: 这本书将主人公描述为勇敢而善良的。
words.en: To describe the character or qualities of someone or something.

words.ex: He has a chronic cough that lasts for months.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个持续数月的慢性咳嗽。
words.en: A chronic illness or condition lasts for a long time and cannot be cured, but it can usually be controlled.

words.ex: The teacher will classify the students by age.
words.ex_cn: 老师将按年龄对学生进行分类。
words.en: To classify things means to divide them into groups or types so that things with similar characteristics are in the same group.

words.tr:
n. 群；团；簇；
v. 聚集；
words.ex: The stars form a bright cluster in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 星星在夜空中形成了一群明亮的星群。
words.en: A cluster of things or people is a small group of them close together.

words.ex: His speech was coherent and easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲连贯且易于理解。
words.en: If something is coherent, it is well planned, so that it is clear and sensible and all its parts go well with each other.

words.ex: The team showed cohesive behavior during the project.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队在项目期间表现出有凝聚力的行为。
words.en: If something is cohesive, it consists of parts that fit together well and form a united whole.

words.tr:
adj. 集体的；
n. 集体；
words.ex: The collective decision was made by all members.
words.ex_cn: 这个集体决定是由所有成员做出的。
words.en: done or shared by all members of a group of people

words.tr: adj. 可比较的；比得上的；类似的；
words.ex: The prices of these two phones are comparable.
words.ex_cn: 这两部手机的价格是可比较的。
words.en: Something that is comparable to something else is similar in size, amount, or quality.

words.ex: This is a comparative study of two languages.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个关于两种语言的比较研究。
words.en: You use comparative to show that you are judging something against a previous or different situation. For example, if you say that something is comparative luxury, you mean that it is luxurious compared to something else.

words.tr: adj. 兼容的；可和谐共存的；
words.ex: This printer is compatible with my computer.
words.ex_cn: 这个打印机与我的电脑兼容。
words.en: If things, for example, systems, ideas, and beliefs, are compatible, they work well together or can exist together successfully.

words.tr: adj. 有竞争力的；竞争的；
words.ex: She is a competitive runner who wins many races.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个有竞争力的跑步者，赢得了许多比赛。
words.en: Competitive is used to describe situations or activities in which people or firms compete with each other.

words.tr: n. 完整性; 完全; 完全性
words.ex: The completeness of the report impressed the board.
words.ex_cn: 报告的完整性给董事会留下了深刻的印象。
words.en: The state or condition of having all necessary or normal parts, components, or steps; the state of being whole and having no parts missing.

words.tr:
adj. 复杂的；
n. 综合楼（群）；
words.ex: The instructions are too complex for children.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明对孩子来说太复杂了。
words.en: Something that is complex has many different parts, and is therefore often difficult to understand.

words.ex: The math problem is complicated.
words.ex_cn: 这个数学问题很复杂。
words.en: Involving many different and confusing aspects.

words.ex: The injury led to a complication in his recovery.
words.ex_cn: 这次受伤使他的康复过程复杂化了。
words.en: A complication is a problem or difficulty that makes a situation harder to deal with.

words.ex: The teacher gave a comprehensive review before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 老师在考试前给了一个全面的复习。
words.en: Something that is comprehensive includes everything that is needed or relevant.

words.ex: Wearing a helmet is compulsory for cyclists.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔是必须的。
words.en: If something is compulsory, you must do it because of a rule or law.

words.tr: prep. 关于； v. “concern”的现在分词；
words.ex: The book is concerning climate change.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是关于气候变化的。
words.en: If something is concerning, it causes you to feel concerned about it.

words.tr:
n. 混凝土；
adj. 具体的；
words.ex: The workers poured concrete to build the foundation.
words.ex_cn: 工人们浇筑混凝土来建造地基。
words.en: Concrete is a hard, strong construction material made by mixing a cementing material (such as Portland cement) and a mineral aggregate (such as sand and gravel) with sufficient water to cause the cement to set and bind the entire mass. In a broader sense, concrete can also refer to something that is tangible, specific, or real.

words.ex: The document is confidential and cannot be shared.
words.ex_cn: 这份文件是机密的，不能分享。
words.en: If you talk to someone in a confidential way, you talk to them quietly because what you are saying is secret or private.

words.ex: He missed three consecutive days of school.
words.ex_cn: 他连续三天没上学。
words.en: Consecutive events, numbers, etc. follow one after another without an interruption.

words.ex: He has a considerable amount of money.
words.ex_cn: 他有相当多的钱。
words.en: Considerable means large in size, amount, or extent.

words.tr: adj. 考虑周到的；体贴的；
words.ex: He is considerate and always asks if others need help.
words.ex_cn: 他很体贴，总是问别人是否需要帮助。
words.en: Someone who is considerate pays attention to the needs, wishes, or feelings of other people.

words.ex: He gave careful consideration to his decision.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的决定进行了仔细考虑。
words.en: Consideration is the process of giving careful thought to something before making a decision or taking action. It also refers to the quality of being thoughtful towards the needs and feelings of others.

words.tr: adj. 一致的；始终如一的；
words.ex: His answers are consistent with the data.
words.ex_cn: 他的答案与数据一致。
words.en: Someone who is consistent always behaves in the same way, has the same attitudes towards people or things, or achieves the same level of success in something.

words.ex: The red hat was conspicuous in the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 那顶红帽子在人群中非常显眼。
words.en: Something that is conspicuous is very obvious or easy to notice.

words.tr: adj. 恒定的；不变的；持续的；
words.ex: The temperature is constant in this room.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间的温度是恒定的。
words.en: Something that is constant happens all the time or is always there.

words.tr:
n. 成分；
adj. 构成的；
words.ex: Sugar is a constituent of soda.
words.ex_cn: 糖是苏打水的一种成分。
words.en: A constituent is a part of a whole. In politics, a constituent is a person who is represented by an elected official.

words.ex: Five apples constitute a basket.
words.ex_cn: 五个苹果构成一篮子。
words.en: If something constitutes a particular thing, it can be regarded as being that thing.

words.tr: adj. 现代的；当代的；同时代的；
words.ex: This museum displays contemporary art.
words.ex_cn: 这个博物馆展示现代艺术。
words.en: Belonging to or occurring in the present; or a person or thing living or existing at the same time as another.

words.ex: There was a contention between the two students about the answer.
words.ex_cn: 两个学生对答案发生了争论。
words.en: A contention is a strong disagreement or argument about something. It can also refer to a point or statement that someone argues is true.

words.ex: The continual rain made the road very muddy.
words.ex_cn: 不停的雨让道路变得非常泥泞。
words.en: Something that is continual happens repeatedly over a period of time.

words.ex: The rain was continuous all day.
words.ex_cn: 雨一整天都在下个不停。
words.en: Something that is continuous happens or exists without stopping or being interrupted.

words.tr:
n. 相反；
adj. 相反的；
words.ex: The contrary of hot is cold.
words.ex_cn: 热的相反是冷。
words.en: If you say that something is true contrary to other people's beliefs or opinions, you are emphasizing that it is true and that they are wrong.

words.tr:
n. 对照；反差；对立；
v. 对比；和...形成对照；
words.ex: The contrast between light and dark is clear in the photo.
words.ex_cn: 这张照片中明暗的对照很明显。
words.en: A contrast is a great difference between two or more things which is clear when you compare them.

words.ex: The movie is controversial because it shows violence.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影因为展示暴力而有争议。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as controversial, you mean that they are the subject of intense public argument, disagreement, or disapproval.

words.ex: The store is open 24 hours for your convenience.
words.ex_cn: 商店24小时营业，以方便您。
words.en: The state of being able to proceed with something with little effort or difficulty.

words.ex: This store is convenient for buying groceries.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店买杂货很方便。
words.en: If something is convenient, it is easy to use or do, or it is useful and suitable for a particular purpose.

words.ex: He wears conventional clothes to work.
words.ex_cn: 他穿传统服装去上班。
words.en: Conventional ideas, methods, or systems are the ones that are generally accepted and used, and that have been used for a long time.

words.ex: He likes coffee; conversely, she prefers tea.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢咖啡；相反，她更喜欢茶。
words.en: In a way that is the opposite or reverse of something else.

words.tr:
adj. 合作的；
n. 合作社；
words.ex: The two companies made a cooperative effort to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 两家公司合作努力解决问题。
words.en: A cooperative is an organization or business that is owned and run jointly by its members, who share the profits or benefits.

words.ex: She coordinates the team's schedule.
words.ex_cn: 她协调团队的安排。
words.en: If you coordinate an activity, you organize the various people and things involved in it. If you coordinate the different parts of your body, you make them work together efficiently.

words.tr: adj. 相应的； v. 符合；“correspond”的现在分词；
words.ex: Each input has a corresponding output.
words.ex_cn: 每个输入都有一个相应的输出。
words.en: If two things are corresponding, they are similar or equivalent in some way, often because they are connected or related in a particular context.

words.ex: The cosmic rays come from outer space.
words.ex_cn: 宇宙射线来自外太空。
words.en: Relating to the universe or cosmos, especially as distinct from the earth.

words.ex: The main criterion for winning is fairness.
words.ex_cn: 获胜的主要标准是公平。
words.en: A criterion is a principle or standard by which something may be judged or decided.

words.tr: adj. 至关重要的；决定性的；
words.ex: It is crucial to drink water every day.
words.ex_cn: 每天喝水至关重要。
words.en: If you describe something as crucial, you mean it is extremely important.

words.ex: The cruelty of the bully made the child cry.
words.ex_cn: 这个欺凌者的残忍让那个孩子哭了。
words.en: Cruelty is behaviour that deliberately causes pain or distress to people or animals.

words.ex: It is customary to shake hands when you meet someone.
words.ex_cn: 见面时握手是习惯做法。
words.en: Something that is customary is normal because it is the way something is usually done.

words.ex: He spends hours in cyberspace every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天在虚拟空间里花几个小时。
words.en: Cyberspace is the notional environment in which communication over computer networks occurs.

words.ex: The rain dampened the sound of the drums.
words.ex_cn: 雨减弱了鼓声。
words.en: To dampen something means to make it slightly wet, or to make it less strong or intense.

words.ex: He gave a definite answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了肯定的答案。
words.en: If something is definite, it is firm and clear, and unlikely to be changed.

words.ex: The dictionary gives a clear definition of the word.
words.ex_cn: 词典给出了这个词的清晰定义。
words.en: A statement of the exact meaning of a word, phrase, or concept.

words.tr: adj. 精致的；微妙的；易碎的；脆弱的；
words.ex: She wore a delicate lace dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条精致的蕾丝连衣裙去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is delicate is small and beautifully shaped. It can also be easily broken or damaged.

words.tr: adv. 美味地；芬香地；令人愉悦地
words.ex: She cooked the meal deliciously.
words.ex_cn: 她把饭菜做得非常美味。
words.en: In a manner that is highly pleasing to the senses, especially taste or smell.

words.ex: The symbol x denotes an unknown number.
words.ex_cn: 符号 x 表示一个未知数。
words.en: If one thing denotes another, it is a sign or indication of it.

words.ex: The train's destination is Beijing.
words.ex_cn: 这列火车的目的地是北京。
words.en: The place to which someone or something is going or being sent.

words.ex: The storm was destructive and broke many houses.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴具有破坏性，摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: Causing great and irreparable harm or damage.

words.ex: This color differs from that one.
words.ex_cn: 这个颜色和那个不同。
words.en: If two or more things differ, they are unlike each other in some way.

words.ex: Can you differentiate between the two colors?
words.ex_cn: 你能区分这两种颜色吗？
words.en: To differentiate means to recognize or express the difference between things or people.

words.ex: The earthquake caused a big disaster.
words.ex_cn: 地震造成了一场大灾难。
words.en: A disaster is an unexpected event causing great damage, destruction, or distress.

words.ex: The storm caused disastrous damage to the village.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴给村庄造成了灾难性的破坏。
words.en: If you describe something as disastrous, you mean that it is very unfortunate or unsuccessful.

words.ex: There is a discrepancy between the two reports.
words.ex_cn: 这两份报告之间有差异。
words.en: A discrepancy is a difference between two or more things that should be the same.

words.ex: The distance between the two towns is 10 kilometers.
words.ex_cn: 两个城镇之间的距离是10公里。
words.en: The amount of space between two places or things.

words.ex: The mountains look distant from here.
words.ex_cn: 从这里看，山显得很远。
words.en: If you describe something as distant, you mean that it is far away in space or time.

words.tr: n. 区别；区分；优等评分；
words.ex: There is a clear distinction between right and wrong.
words.ex_cn: 对与错之间有明显的区别。
words.en: A distinction is a difference or contrast between similar things or people.

words.ex: The two colors distinguish the two teams.
words.ex_cn: 这两种颜色使两个队伍有所不同。
words.en: If you can distinguish one thing from another, you can see or understand how they are different.

words.ex: The noise from the construction caused a disturbance.
words.ex_cn: 建筑工地的噪音造成了干扰。
words.en: A disturbance is an event or situation in which people behave in a noisy or violent way, or something that interrupts what you are doing.

words.tr: adj. 不同的；多种多样的；
words.ex: The class has diverse students from many countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个班级有来自许多国家的不同学生。
words.en: If a group or range of things is diverse, it is made up of a wide variety of things.

words.ex: The road was diverted around the park.
words.ex_cn: 这条路被改道绕过公园。
words.en: If you divert someone or something, you cause them to change direction or to go somewhere different.

words.tr: adj. 家庭的；国内的；驯养的；
words.ex: She prefers domestic chores over going out.
words.ex_cn: 她更喜欢做家务而不是外出。
words.en: Domestic means relating to the home, family, or household affairs. It can also refer to something that is made or produced within a country and not imported.

words.ex: The cat sat in the doorway.
words.ex_cn: 猫坐在门口。
words.en: A doorway is the space in a wall where a door opens and closes, or the covered area just outside a door.

words.tr: v. （使）调低速档；（使）工作降格，下调职业档次；减慢节奏（以减轻压力）; n. 换低速档；（质量...
words.ex: He downshifted to slow down the car.
words.ex_cn: 他降档以减慢车速。
words.en: To downshift means to change to a lower gear in a vehicle, or to reduce the speed or intensity of an activity.

words.tr:
adv. 向下地；
adj. 向下的；
words.ex: The leaves fell downward slowly.
words.ex_cn: 树叶慢慢向下飘落。
words.en: Moving or leading towards a lower place or level

words.ex: The company made drastic cuts to save money.
words.ex_cn: 公司进行了急剧的削减以节省资金。
words.en: If you describe a change or action as drastic, you mean that it is extreme and often severe.

words.ex: He became a dropout after failing math class.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学考试不及格后退学了。
words.en: A dropout is a person who leaves school or college before they have finished their studies, especially because they are not interested in continuing.

words.ex: He looked dubiously at the cheap watch.
words.ex_cn: 他怀疑地看着那块便宜的手表。
words.en: In a manner that hesitates or doubts; with doubt or uncertainty.

words.tr: v. 复制；复印；再做一次；
words.ex: He duplicated the file to save a copy.
words.ex_cn: 他复制了该文件以保存一份副本。
words.en: To duplicate something means to make an exact copy of it.

words.ex: This bag is durable and lasts for years.
words.ex_cn: 这个包很耐用，可以用很多年。
words.en: Something that is durable is strong and lasts a long time without breaking or becoming weaker.

words.ex: The fairy tale features a dwarf who lives in a small house.
words.ex_cn: 这个童话故事中有一个住在小房子里的侏儒。
words.en: A dwarf is a person, animal, or plant that is much smaller than the usual size of its species. As a verb, to dwarf means to make someone or something seem small or insignificant in comparison.

words.tr:
adj. 动态的；有活力的；不断变化的；
n. 活力；动力；
words.ex: The game has dynamic weather that changes every hour.
words.ex_cn: 这个游戏有每小时变化的动态天气。
words.en: If you describe someone as dynamic, you approve of them because they are full of energy or full of new ideas.

words.ex: The children are eager to open their presents.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们渴望打开他们的礼物。
words.en: If you are eager to do or have something, you want to do or have it very much.

words.ex: The eastern city has many old temples.
words.ex_cn: 东部的城市有许多古老的寺庙。
words.en: Eastern means in or from the east part of an area.

words.ex: He is an eccentric man who wears socks with sandals.
words.ex_cn: 他是个古怪的人，穿着袜子配凉鞋。
words.en: If you say that someone is eccentric, you mean that they behave in a strange way, and have habits or opinions that are different from those of most people.

words.ex: This car is economical because it uses little fuel.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车很经济，因为它耗油少。
words.en: Using money, resources, or time in a careful and effective way.

words.tr: adj. 可食用的；可以吃的；
words.ex: These mushrooms are edible and safe to eat.
words.ex_cn: 这些蘑菇是可食用的，安全可以吃。
words.en: Fit to be eaten as food.

words.tr:
n. 社论；
adj. 编辑的；
words.ex: The newspaper published an editorial about climate change.
words.ex_cn: 报纸发表了一篇关于气候变化的社论。
words.en: An editorial is an article in a newspaper which gives the opinion of the editor or publisher on a topic or item of news.

words.ex: He uses an efficient way to solve math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他用一种高效的方法解决数学问题。
words.en: If something or someone is efficient, they are able to do tasks successfully, without wasting time or energy.

words.ex: The elderly man walks slowly with a cane.
words.ex_cn: 这位年老的男子拄着拐杖慢慢走。
words.en: An elderly person is someone who is old or aging.

words.ex: He fixed the electrical wire with tape.
words.ex_cn: 他用胶带修好了电线。
words.en: Relating to electricity or things that use electricity.

words.ex: She wore an elegant dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条优雅的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe a person or thing as elegant, you mean that they are pleasing and graceful in appearance or style.

words.ex: He is learning elementary math at school.
words.ex_cn: 他在学校学习初级数学。
words.en: Elementary means relating to the simplest and most basic aspects of a subject.

words.ex: The elite of the city often meet at private clubs.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市的精英经常在私人俱乐部会面。
words.en: You can refer to the most powerful, rich, or talented people within a particular group, place, or society as the elite.

words.tr: adj. 雄辩的；有口才的；有说服力的
words.ex: He gave an eloquent speech at the ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 他在仪式上发表了富有感染力的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as eloquent, you mean that they are able to express their ideas and opinions well, so that other people understand them and are influenced by them.

words.ex: I can't find my keys here; they must be elsewhere.
words.ex_cn: 我在这儿找不到我的钥匙，它们一定在别处。
words.en: In or to some other place; not here.

words.ex: He called an emergency doctor when he felt sick.
words.ex_cn: 当他感到不舒服时，他叫了急诊医生。
words.en: An emergency is an unexpected and usually dangerous situation that calls for immediate action.

words.ex: He is an eminent scientist who won the Nobel Prize.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位获得诺贝尔奖的杰出科学家。
words.en: An eminent person is well-known and respected, especially because they are good at their profession.

words.tr: adj. 经验主义的；以经验为根据的；
words.ex: The scientist used empirical data to support her theory.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家使用经验数据来支持她的理论。
words.en: Empirical evidence or study relies on practical experience rather than theories.

words.ex: He built his endurance by running every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他通过每天早晨跑步来增强耐力。
words.en: The ability to endure an unpleasant or difficult process or situation without giving up.

words.ex: He had to endure the cold winter without a coat.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不在没有外套的情况下忍受寒冷的冬天。
words.en: To endure means to suffer something difficult, unpleasant, or painful, or to continue to exist for a long time.

words.ex: The enforcement of traffic laws keeps roads safe.
words.ex_cn: 交通法规的执行使道路更安全。
words.en: The act of compelling observance of or compliance with a law, rule, or obligation.

words.ex: Exercise can enhance your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以提高你的健康。
words.en: To enhance something means to improve its value, quality, or attractiveness.

words.ex: The elephant is enormous.
words.ex_cn: 这头大象非常巨大。
words.en: If you describe something as enormous, you are emphasizing that it is extremely large in size or amount.

words.tr: adj. 充满热情的；热心的；
words.ex: He is enthusiastic about playing basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他对打篮球充满热情。
words.en: If you are enthusiastic about something, you show how much you like or enjoy it by the way that you behave and talk.

words.tr: adj. 全部的；整个的；完全的；
words.ex: He ate the entire cake.
words.ex_cn: 他吃掉了整个蛋糕。
words.en: You use entire to emphasize that you are referring to the whole of something, for example, the whole of a place, time, or population.

words.ex: The epidemic spread quickly across the country.
words.ex_cn: 这种流行病迅速蔓延到全国。
words.en: An epidemic is a large number of cases of an infectious disease occurring at the same time.

words.tr: n. 事件；一集；一段经历；
words.ex: The accident was a sad episode in his life.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故是他生命中的一件悲伤的事。
words.en: An episode is a part of a story that is broadcast on television or radio as one of a series, or a single event or group of related events.

words.ex: The invention of the internet changed our era.
words.ex_cn: 互联网的发明改变了我们的时代。
words.en: An era is a period of time that is considered as a single unit because of a particular characteristic or event.

words.ex: His answer was erroneous because he added wrong.
words.ex_cn: 他的答案是错误的，因为他加错了。
words.en: If you describe someone's beliefs or opinions as erroneous, you mean that they are incorrect and based on false information.

words.tr: adj. 必需的；基本的；本质的；
words.ex: Water is essential for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命是必需的。
words.en: Something that is essential is extremely important or absolutely necessary to a particular subject, situation, or activity.

words.ex: The stars seem eternal in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中的星星看起来是永久的。
words.en: If something is eternal, it lasts forever.

words.ex: It is evident that he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 很明显他很累。
words.en: If something is evident, it is easy to see, perceive, or understand.

words.ex: The bird evolved from a small dinosaur.
words.ex_cn: 这种鸟由一种小型恐龙演变而来。
words.en: If something evolves or you evolve it, it gradually develops over a period of time into something different and usually more advanced.

words.ex: He gave the exact time of the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了会议的确切时间。
words.en: If you describe something as exact, you mean that it is precise and accurate in all its details.

words.tr: adj. 卓越的；杰出的；罕见的；特别的；
words.ex: She is an exceptional student who always gets top grades.
words.ex_cn: 她是一名卓越的学生，总是取得最高分。
words.en: An exceptional person or thing has some unusual quality or ability that makes them different from others.

words.ex: This brand has an exclusive design.
words.ex_cn: 这个品牌拥有独有的设计。
words.en: Something that is exclusive is available only to particular people, and not to everyone.

words.tr: adj. 外来的；外国来的；奇异的；
words.ex: The market sells exotic fruits from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个市场出售来自其他国家的外来水果。
words.en: Something that is exotic is unusual and interesting because it comes from or is related to a distant country.

words.ex: He gave an explicit answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了明确的答案。
words.en: Something that is explicit is expressed or shown clearly and openly, without any attempt to hide anything.

words.ex: The worker had long exposure to loud noise.
words.ex_cn: 这名工人长期暴露在噪音中。
words.en: The condition of being exposed to something, especially to something harmful or unpleasant.

words.ex: His expression showed he was happy.
words.ex_cn: 他的表情显示他很快乐。
words.en: The act of making your thoughts, feelings, etc., known by speech, writing, or some other method.

words.tr: adj. 广大的；广阔的；广泛的；大量的；
words.ex: He has extensive knowledge of history.
words.ex_cn: 他拥有广博的历史知识。
words.en: Something that is extensive covers a wide area or includes a lot of things.

words.ex: The extent of his knowledge surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的知识广度让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The area or length to which something extends.

words.ex: The exterior of the house is painted white.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子的外观是白色的。
words.en: The outer surface or structure of something.

words.ex: The external wall of the house is painted blue.
words.ex_cn: 房子的外墙被刷成了蓝色。
words.en: External is used to indicate that something is on the outside of a surface or body, or that it exists, happens, or comes from outside.

words.ex: She has an extraordinary talent for music.
words.ex_cn: 她具有非凡的音乐天赋。
words.en: Something that is extraordinary is very unusual or remarkable.

words.ex: He bought an extravagant car that cost too much money.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一辆奢侈的车，价格太贵了。
words.en: Spending much more than is necessary or wise; excessively expensive.

words.tr:
adj. 极度的；
n. 极端；极端的事物；
words.ex: He felt extreme pain after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后感到极度疼痛。
words.en: If you describe something as extreme, you mean that it is very great in degree or intensity.

words.ex: The movie was fairly interesting.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影相当地有趣。
words.en: To a moderately sufficient extent or degree.

words.tr:
n. 仙子；小精灵；
adj. 幻想中的；
words.ex: The little girl saw a fairy in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 小女孩在花园里看到了一位仙子。
words.en: A fairy is a mythical being of folklore and romance usually having magic powers and dwelling on earth in close relationship with humans.

words.tr: adj. 忠实的；虔诚的；可靠的；
words.ex: He is a faithful friend who always helps me.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个总是帮助我的忠实朋友。
words.en: Someone who is faithful remains loyal to a person, belief, or cause, and continues to support them.

words.ex: I am familiar with this song.
words.ex_cn: 我熟悉这首歌。
words.en: If someone or something is familiar to you, you recognize them or know them well.

words.ex: The village suffered from famine last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年这个村庄遭受了饥荒。
words.en: A famine is a serious shortage of food in a country, which may cause many people to get sick or die.

words.tr:
v. 想要；
adj. 花哨的；昂贵的；
n. 爱好；
words.ex: I fancy a cup of tea.
words.ex_cn: 我想要一杯茶。
words.en: If you describe something as fancy, you mean that it is special, unusual, or elaborate, often because it has a lot of decoration or is very expensive.

words.ex: The child loves to play with fantasy stories about dragons.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子喜欢玩关于龙的幻想故事。
words.en: A fantasy is a pleasant situation or event that you imagine, which is unlikely to happen.

words.tr: adj. 有缺陷的；有故障的；有错误的；
words.ex: The faulty phone keeps turning off.
words.ex_cn: 这部有缺陷的手机总是自动关机。
words.en: If you describe something as faulty, you mean that it is not perfect or it has some weaknesses.

words.tr:
adj. 女性的；雌性的；
n. 雌性；女性；
words.ex: The female teacher is very kind.
words.ex_cn: 这位女老师非常和蔼。
words.en: A female is a person or animal that belongs to the sex that can have babies or produce eggs.

words.ex: She has a feminine voice.
words.ex_cn: 她的声音很女性化。
words.en: having qualities or an appearance traditionally associated with women, especially delicacy and prettiness.

words.tr: adj. 肥沃的；有繁殖力的；多产的；富饶的；
words.ex: The fertile land grows many crops.
words.ex_cn: 这片肥沃的土地长满了各种作物。
words.en: Land or soil that is fertile is able to support the growth of a large number of strong healthy plants.

words.tr: adj. 封建的；封建制度的
words.ex: The land was owned by feudal lords.
words.ex_cn: 土地由封建领主拥有。
words.en: Relating to, resembling, or characteristic of feudalism.

words.ex: He loves reading science fiction.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢读科幻小说。
words.en: Fiction refers to literature in the form of prose, especially novels, that describes imaginary events and people.

words.ex: The book has a finite number of pages.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的页数是有限的。
words.en: Something that is finite has a definite fixed size or extent.

words.ex: He gave me a fiver for the bus ticket.
words.ex_cn: 他给了我五英镑买公交车票。
words.en: A fiver is a five-pound note or a five-dollar bill.

words.ex: The cake has a sweet flavor.
words.ex_cn: 这个蛋糕有一种甜味。
words.en: The flavor of a food or drink is its taste, especially a pleasant or distinctive one.

words.ex: She is flexible with her schedule.
words.ex_cn: 她的日程安排很灵活。
words.en: Able to change or be changed easily according to the situation.

words.tr:
adj. 最重要的；
adv. 首要地；
words.ex: He is the foremost expert in this field.
words.ex_cn: 他是这个领域最重要的专家。
words.en: Most important or prominent; leading.

words.ex: The storm was formidable and destroyed many houses.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴很可怕，摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as formidable, you mean that you feel slightly frightened by them because they are very great or impressive.

words.tr: adj. 即将发生（或出版等）的；准备好的；
words.ex: The forthcoming book will be released next month.
words.ex_cn: 即将出版的这本书将在下个月发布。
words.en: If something is forthcoming, it is happening or coming soon.

words.ex: He is fortunate to have a good job.
words.ex_cn: 他很幸运拥有一份好工作。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is fortunate, you mean that they are lucky.

words.tr:
adj. 肮脏恶臭的；
v. 对…犯规；
words.ex: The foul smell came from the garbage bin.
words.ex_cn: 那股恶臭来自垃圾桶。
words.en: If you describe something as foul, you mean it is dirty and smells or tastes unpleasant. In sports, a foul is an act that is against the rules of the game.

words.tr: adj. 脆弱的；易碎的；不牢固的；
words.ex: The glass is fragile and might break easily.
words.ex_cn: 这个玻璃很脆弱，容易碎。
words.en: If something is fragile, it is easily broken or damaged.

words.ex: The garden has fragrant flowers.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园里有芳香的花。
words.en: Having a pleasant or sweet smell.

words.ex: There is friction between the two neighbors over the fence.
words.ex_cn: 两个邻居因为篱笆问题产生了不和。
words.en: The resistance that one surface or object encounters when moving over another.

words.tr:
n. 功能；职责；
v. 起作用；
words.ex: The function of this button is to turn on the light.
words.ex_cn: 这个按钮的功能是打开灯。
words.en: A function is the purpose that something is designed to have or the job that someone is employed to do. It can also refer to a mathematical relationship or a social event.

words.tr: adj. 基本的；基础的；根本的；
words.ex: Water is a fundamental need for life.
words.ex_cn: 水是生命的基本需求。
words.en: You use fundamental to describe things, activities, and principles that are very important or essential. They affect the basic nature of other things or are the most important element upon which other things depend.

words.ex: It was futile to try to fix the broken clock.
words.ex_cn: 试图修理坏掉的钟表是徒劳的。
words.en: If you say that something is futile, you mean there is no point in doing it, usually because it has no chance of succeeding.

words.ex: He bought a gallon of milk from the store.
words.ex_cn: 他从商店买了一加仑牛奶。
words.en: A gallon is a unit of measurement for liquids that is equal to eight pints. In Britain, it is equal to about 4.546 litres. In America, it is equal to about 3.785 litres.

words.tr: n. （有多方面知识和经验的）通才；多面手
words.ex: He is a generalist who works in many areas.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位涉猎多个领域的人。
words.en: A generalist is a person who knows a lot about many different subjects, rather than specializing in one particular subject.

words.ex: My generation grew up with smartphones.
words.ex_cn: 我们这一代人是伴随着智能手机长大的。
words.en: A generation is all the people in a group or country who are of a similar age, especially when they are considered as having the same experiences or attitudes.

words.tr:
adj. 巨大的；伟大的；
n. 巨人；伟人；
words.ex: The giant elephant stood near the tree.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的大象站在树旁。
words.en: A giant is an imaginary person who is very big and strong, especially one mentioned in old stories. In everyday language, a giant can also refer to a very large and successful company or organization.

words.ex: The problem is a global issue.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题是一个全球性的问题。
words.en: relating to the whole world; worldwide

words.ex: She wore a gorgeous dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件华丽的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you say that something is gorgeous, you mean that it gives you a lot of pleasure or is very attractive.

words.ex: She added a gram of salt to the soup.
words.ex_cn: 她往汤里加了一克盐。
words.en: A gram is a unit of weight in the metric system equal to one thousandth of a kilogram.

words.tr:
n. 节目；程序；
v. 编程；
words.ex: We watched a funny program on TV last night.
words.ex_cn: 我们昨晚在电视上看了一个有趣的节目。
words.en: A program is a set of instructions that a computer follows in order to perform a particular task.

words.tr: n. 墓地；坟场；垃圾场；废物堆积处
words.ex: The old graveyard is quiet at night.
words.ex_cn: 那个古老的墓地晚上很安静。
words.en: A graveyard is an area of land, often near a church, where dead people are buried.

words.ex: Follow the guideline to complete the form.
words.ex_cn: 按照指导路线完成表格。
words.en: A guideline is a set of rules or instructions that are given by an official organization telling you how to do something, especially something difficult.

words.tr: n. 栖息地；居留地；产地；
words.ex: The panda's habitat is in the mountains of China.
words.ex_cn: 熊猫的栖息地在中国的山区。
words.en: The natural environment in which a species or group of species lives.

words.ex: He stopped halfway to rest.
words.ex_cn: 他在半路停下来休息。
words.en: At or to a point midway between two others.

words.ex: The teacher gave us a handbook for the science project.
words.ex_cn: 老师给我们发了一本科学项目的手册。
words.en: A handbook is a type of reference work, or other collection of instructions, that is intended to provide ready reference.

words.ex: A handful of students stayed after class to ask questions.
words.ex_cn: 少数学生课后留下来提问。
words.en: A handful of something is a small amount of it, especially when it is not enough or when it is difficult to manage.

words.tr:
n. 残疾；障碍；阻碍；不利
v. 妨碍；使不利
words.ex: He has a physical handicap but still runs every day.
words.ex_cn: 他有身体残疾，但仍然每天跑步。
words.en: A handicap is a condition that markedly restricts a person's ability to function physically, mentally, or socially.

words.ex: The music heightens the feeling of sadness.
words.ex_cn: 音乐加深了悲伤的感觉。
words.en: If something heightens a feeling or if the feeling heightens, the feeling increases in degree or intensity.

words.ex: We eat homegrown vegetables from our garden.
words.ex_cn: 我们吃来自自家菜园的本土蔬菜。
words.en: Homegrown refers to something that is grown or produced in one's own country or locality, rather than being imported.

words.ex: Honesty is important in friendship.
words.ex_cn: 诚实在友谊中很重要。
words.en: The quality of being honest, which involves being truthful, sincere, and free from deceit or fraud.

words.ex: The car has 200 horsepower.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车有200马力。
words.en: A unit of power equal to 550 foot-pounds per second (about 750 watts), used in measuring the power of engines or motors.

words.ex: The two shirts are identical.
words.ex_cn: 这两件衬衫是一样的。
words.en: Exactly the same, or very similar.

words.ex: The mountain is immense.
words.ex_cn: 这座山非常巨大。
words.en: Extremely large or great, especially in scale or degree.

words.ex: The importance of homework is clear.
words.ex_cn: 作业的重要性是显而易见的。
words.en: The quality or state of being important; significance.

words.ex: The incidence of flu increased last winter.
words.ex_cn: 去年冬天流感的发生率上升了。
words.en: The incidence of something is the frequency with which it occurs or the rate at which it happens.

words.ex: His income is enough to pay for rent and food.
words.ex_cn: 他的收入足以支付房租和食物。
words.en: Income is the money that a person or a company earns regularly, for example from investment or work.

words.ex: He is tired, and indeed he fell asleep quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他很累，的确很快就睡着了。
words.en: You use indeed to confirm or agree with something that has just been said.

words.ex: Water is indispensable for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命是必不可少的。
words.en: Absolutely necessary or essential.

words.ex: Each student must complete the task individually.
words.ex_cn: 每个学生必须单独完成任务。
words.en: If something is done individually, it is done separately to each person or thing in a group.

words.tr: n. 产业主义，工业主义；工业制度
words.ex: The rise of industrialism marked a new era in economic development.
words.ex_cn: 工业主义的兴起标志着经济发展的新时代。
words.en: Industrialism is the social and economic system based on industrial production or industry.

words.ex: The ball keeps moving because of inertia.
words.ex_cn: 球因为惯性继续移动。
words.en: Inertia is the tendency of a physical object to continue moving in a straight line at a constant speed, or to stay at rest, unless it is acted upon by a force.

words.tr: adj. 不可避免的；必定的；
words.ex: It is inevitable that the sun will rise tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 太阳明天一定会升起。
words.en: If something is inevitable, it is certain to happen and cannot be prevented or avoided.

words.tr: adj. 传染性的；有感染力的；
words.ex: The virus is infectious and spreads quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒具有传染性，传播迅速。
words.en: An infectious disease can be passed from one person to another, especially through the air they breathe.

words.ex: This product is inferior to the other one.
words.ex_cn: 这个产品比另一个差。
words.en: If one person or thing is inferior to another, they are not as good, important, or valuable as the other person or thing.

words.ex: He is an influential teacher in our school.
words.ex_cn: 他是我们学校一位有影响力的老师。
words.en: Having great influence on someone or something.

words.ex: Honesty is an inherent quality of a good leader.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是好领导固有的品质。
words.en: Existing in something as a permanent, essential, or characteristic attribute.

words.tr:
adj. 最初的；开始的；
n. 首字母；
words.ex: This is the initial plan for the project.
words.ex_cn: 这是这个项目的最初计划。
words.en: The first letter of a name or word, used to represent the whole name or word.

words.tr:
adj. 内陆的；
adv. 向内地；在内陆；
n. 内地；内陆；
words.ex: The small village is located inland, far from the sea.
words.ex_cn: 这个小村庄位于内陆，远离大海。
words.en: Inland means situated in the interior of a country rather than on the coast.

words.ex: There are innumerable stars in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中有数不清的星星。
words.en: Too many to be counted; very many.

words.ex: He paid the first installment last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周支付了第一期分期付款。
words.en: An installment is one of the amounts, usually equal, into which a debt is divided for payment at stated intervals over a fixed period.

words.ex: She instinctively reached for her phone when it rang.
words.ex_cn: 电话响时，她下意识地伸手去拿手机。
words.en: If you behave instinctively, you do something without thinking about it because it seems natural or the right thing to do.

words.tr: adj. 有帮助的；乐器的；仪器的；
words.ex: Her advice was instrumental in helping me pass the exam.
words.ex_cn: 她的建议对帮助我通过考试很有帮助。
words.en: If someone or something is instrumental in a process, plan, or system, they are one of the most important influences in causing it to happen.

words.ex: The vase remained intact after the fall.
words.ex_cn: 花瓶从高处摔下后依然完整无缺。
words.en: Something that is intact is complete and has not been damaged or changed.

words.tr: adj. 可理解的；明白易懂的；清楚的
words.ex: His explanation was intelligible to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的解释人人都能听懂。
words.en: Capable of being understood; comprehensible.

words.tr: adj. 暂时的；临时的；期间的；
words.ex: He is the interim manager until a new one is hired.
words.ex_cn: 在招聘到新的经理之前，他是临时经理。
words.en: An interim is a period of time between one event, process, or period and another, especially one of temporary nature.

words.tr:
n. 内部；
adj. 内部的；
words.ex: The interior of the house is very cozy.
words.ex_cn: 房子的内部非常舒适。
words.en: The interior of something is the inside part of it.

words.ex: He is an intermediate student in English.
words.ex_cn: 他是英语的中级学生。
words.en: An intermediate stage, level, or position is one that occurs between two other stages, levels, or positions.

words.ex: The internal parts of the machine need repair.
words.ex_cn: 机器的内部零件需要修理。
words.en: Internal is used to describe things that exist or happen inside a particular person, object, or place.

words.ex: The lock has an intricate design.
words.ex_cn: 这个锁有复杂的结构。
words.en: You use intricate to describe something that has many small parts or details.

words.tr: adj. 固有的；内在的；本身的；
words.ex: Honesty is an intrinsic part of her character.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是她性格中固有的部分。
words.en: belonging to a thing by its very nature

words.ex: The mistake will invalidate the result.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误会使结果无效。
words.en: To invalidate something such as a contract or an election means to make it officially not valid.

words.tr: adj. 无价的；非常宝贵的；
words.ex: Her advice was invaluable to me.
words.ex_cn: 她的建议对我而言是无价的。
words.en: If you describe something as invaluable, you mean that it is extremely useful.

words.ex: He is invariably late for meetings.
words.ex_cn: 他总是开会迟到。
words.en: If something invariably happens or is invariably true, it always happens or is always true.

words.ex: The store made an inventory of all the products.
words.ex_cn: 商店对所有商品做了一份清单。
words.en: An inventory is a detailed list of all the items in a place.

words.ex: The ghost is invisible to the human eye.
words.ex_cn: 这个鬼魂肉眼看不见。
words.en: If something is invisible, you cannot see it because it is hidden or because it is very difficult to see.

words.ex: The ship sailed inward toward the harbor.
words.ex_cn: 船向港口内航行。
words.en: Directed or moving towards the inside; relating to the inside or inner part of something.

words.ex: He gave a justification for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他为迟到提供了一个正当的理由。
words.en: A justification for something is an acceptable reason or explanation for it.

words.ex: I haven't seen him lately.
words.ex_cn: 我最近没见到他。
words.en: If you say that something has happened lately, you mean that it has happened recently.

words.tr: adj. 最重要的；一流的；处于领导地位的； v. “lead”的现在分词；带领；领导；
words.ex: He is the leading scientist in this field.
words.ex_cn: 他是这个领域最重要的科学家。
words.en: If something is leading in a particular area, it is the most important or advanced thing in that area.

words.ex: He is literally the best player on the team.
words.ex_cn: 他确实是队里最好的球员。
words.en: In a literal manner or sense; exactly.

words.tr: adj. 未固定牢的；宽松的；
words.ex: The loose screw fell off the table.
words.ex_cn: 那个松动的螺丝从桌子上掉了下来。
words.en: Not firmly or tightly fixed in place; detached or able to be detached.

words.ex: The sunset over the mountains was magnificent.
words.ex_cn: 山上的日落壮丽极了。
words.en: If you say that something or someone is magnificent, you mean that you think they are extremely good, beautiful, or impressive.

words.ex: The majority of students like pizza.
words.ex_cn: 大多数学生喜欢披萨。
words.en: The majority is the greater number or part of something.

words.ex: He wore a scary mask at the Halloween party.
words.ex_cn: 他在万圣节派对上戴了一个可怕的面具。
words.en: A mask is a piece of cloth or other material that you wear over your face to hide or protect it.

words.tr: adj. 大规模的；大而重的；
words.ex: The company launched a massive advertising campaign.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司发起了一场大规模的广告活动。
words.en: Something that is massive is extremely large in size, amount, or extent.

words.tr:
n. 事情；物质；
v. 要紧；
words.ex: What's the matter with you?
words.ex_cn: 你怎么了？
words.en: Matter is a physical substance in general, as distinct from mind and spirit; (in physics) that which occupies space and possesses rest mass, especially as distinct from energy. It can also refer to a subject or situation under consideration.

words.ex: The weather is mild today.
words.ex_cn: 今天天气温和。
words.en: Mild is used to describe something that is not extreme, severe, or strong, such as weather, taste, or behavior.

words.tr:
adj. 微型的；
n. 微型画；小型模型；
words.ex: He bought a miniature car for his collection.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的收藏买了一辆微型汽车。
words.en: A miniature is a very small detailed painting, often a portrait. It can also refer to a small-scale model or representation of something.

words.tr:
v. 呻吟；呼啸；抱怨
n. 呻吟声；萧萧声；抱怨
words.ex: He moans when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 他累了的时候会呻吟。
words.en: If you moan, you make a low sound, usually because you are unhappy or in pain.

words.tr:
v. 嘲笑；嘲弄；
adj. 仿制的；
words.ex: They mock him for his accent.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为他口音而嘲笑他。
words.en: To mock someone means to laugh at them, tease them, or make them look foolish, often by imitating their behavior or speech.

words.ex: The team gained momentum after scoring the first goal.
words.ex_cn: 球队在进第一个球后获得了势头。
words.en: Momentum is the ability of something to keep increasing, developing, or being more successful.

words.ex: A multitude of people attended the festival.
words.ex_cn: 大量的人参加了这个节日。
words.en: A multitude of things or people is a very large number of them.

words.tr:
n. 低语声；嘟哝
v. 低语；咕哝；私下抱怨
words.ex: I heard a murmur from the next room.
words.ex_cn: 我听到隔壁房间传来低语声。
words.en: A murmur is a low, indistinct, continuous sound, as of a stream or of voices.

words.tr:
v. 咕哝地抱怨；嘀咕
n. 咕哝地抱怨；嘀咕
words.ex: He mutters under his breath when he is angry.
words.ex_cn: 当他生气时，他会低声嘟囔。
words.en: To speak or say something in a low voice that is hard to hear, often because you are annoyed or complaining.

words.ex: The child gave a naive smile when he believed the story.
words.ex_cn: 当孩子相信这个故事时，他露出了天真的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as naïve, you think they lack experience and so expect things to be easy or people to be honest or kind.

words.ex: The child was naked in the bathtub.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在浴缸里是裸体的。
words.en: If something is naked, it is not covered by anything such as clothes or paint.

words.ex: The weather today is nasty and rainy.
words.ex_cn: 今天的天气令人不愉快，又阴又雨。
words.en: If you describe something as nasty, you mean it is very unpleasant, unattractive, or unkind.

words.tr: adj. 整洁的；整齐的；有条理的
words.ex: He keeps his desk neat.
words.ex_cn: 他保持书桌整洁。
words.en: Neat things are tidy, smart, or carefully arranged.

words.ex: The rain necessitated staying indoors.
words.ex_cn: 下雨使待在室内成为必需。
words.en: To necessitate something means to make it necessary for something to be done or to happen.

words.ex: Water is a basic necessity for life.
words.ex_cn: 水是生命的基本必需品。
words.en: Something that is necessary or indispensable.

words.ex: The error is negligible.
words.ex_cn: 这个误差可以忽略。
words.en: If you describe something as negligible, you mean that it is so small or unimportant that it is not worth considering or worrying about.

words.ex: The noise from the street kept me awake.
words.ex_cn: 街道上的噪声让我睡不着。
words.en: Noise is a sound, especially one that is loud, unpleasant, or disturbing.

words.ex: He accepted a nominal fee for the service.
words.ex_cn: 他为这项服务收取了微不足道的费用。
words.en: If you say that something is nominal, you mean that it is very small in comparison to the real value or importance of something.

words.ex: His temperature is normal.
words.ex_cn: 他的体温正常。
words.en: Something that is normal is usual and ordinary, and is what people expect.

words.ex: The northern wind is cold in winter.
words.ex_cn: 冬天的北风很冷。
words.en: Northern means situated in, directed towards, or facing the north.

words.tr:
n. 注意；通知；
v. 注意；留心；通知；
words.ex: He gave a notice about the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他发布了关于会议的通知。
words.en: If you notice something or someone, you become aware of them.

words.ex: The change in her mood was noticeable.
words.ex_cn: 她情绪的变化显而易见。
words.en: Something that is noticeable is very obvious, so that it is easy to see, hear, or recognize.

words.ex: The teacher will notify the students about the test.
words.ex_cn: 老师会通知学生们关于考试的事。
words.en: If you notify someone of something, you officially inform them about it.

words.tr:
n. （长篇）小说；
adj. 新颖的；新奇的；
words.ex: He wrote a novel about a brave girl.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一部关于一个勇敢女孩的小说。
words.en: A novel is a long written story about imaginary people and events.

words.ex: The test has only numerical answers.
words.ex_cn: 这个测试只有数字答案。
words.en: Numerical means relating to numbers or consisting of numbers.

words.ex: There are numerous books on the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 书架上有许多书。
words.en: If people or things are numerous, they exist or are present in large numbers.

words.ex: It is obvious that he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 很明显他很累。
words.en: If something is obvious, it is easy to see or understand.

words.tr: adj. 奇怪的；奇数的；余的；
words.ex: He wore an odd hat to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶奇怪的帽子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as odd, you mean that they are strange or unusual.

words.ex: This temperature is the optimum for growing plants.
words.ex_cn: 这个温度是最适宜植物生长的。
words.en: The optimum is the best or most favorable condition, degree, amount, etc., for achieving a particular result.

words.tr: adj. 普通的；平常的；一般的；
words.ex: He wore an ordinary shirt to school.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了一件普通的衬衫去学校。
words.en: Something that is ordinary is not special or different in any way.

words.ex: He used the sun to orient himself.
words.ex_cn: 他用太阳来确定方向。
words.en: To orient means to align or position something in relation to the points of a compass or other specified positions, or to familiarize someone with a new situation or environment.

words.tr: n. 入学介绍；岗前训练；方向；取向；
words.ex: The school held an orientation for new students on Monday.
words.ex_cn: 学校在周一为新生举行了入学介绍。
words.en: The act of orienting or the state of being oriented; the determination of the relative position of something or someone (especially oneself).

words.tr: n. 出口；发泄途径；经销店；折扣店
words.ex: The river flows out through an outlet.
words.ex_cn: 河水通过一个出口流出。
words.en: An outlet is a hole or pipe through which liquid or air can flow out, or a point in a wall where you can connect electrical equipment to the electricity supply.

words.tr:
adj. 在头顶上的；
adv. 在空中；
words.ex: The overhead light is too bright.
words.ex_cn: 头顶上的灯太亮了。
words.en: You use overhead to indicate that something is above you or above the place that you are talking about.

words.ex: He overheard them talking about the party.
words.ex_cn: 他无意中听到他们在谈论派对。
words.en: To overhear is to hear what someone is saying without them knowing that you are listening.

words.tr: n. 专家咨询组；嵌板；仪器板；
words.ex: The government formed a panel to advise on health policy.
words.ex_cn: 政府组建了一个专家咨询组来就卫生政策提供建议。
words.en: A panel is a small group of people who are chosen to do something, for example to discuss something in public or to make a decision.

words.tr:
adj. 特指的；特殊的；挑剔的；
n. 细节；详情；
words.ex: He wants a particular book, not any other.
words.ex_cn: 他想要一本特指的书，不是别的。
words.en: You use particular to emphasize that you are talking about one thing or one kind of thing rather than other similar ones.

words.ex: The two countries signed a treaty for peace.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家签署了和平条约。
words.en: Peace is a situation or a period of time in which there is no war or violence in a country or an area.

words.ex: The lake is peaceful in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 清晨的湖面很宁静。
words.en: If a time, place, or situation is peaceful, it is quiet and calm, with no violence or trouble.

words.ex: This town has a peculiar custom of dancing at midnight.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇有一个独特的午夜跳舞习俗。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as peculiar, you think that they are strange or unusual, sometimes in an unpleasant way.

words.ex: She bought a new perfume for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对买了一瓶新香水。
words.en: A perfume is a pleasant-smelling liquid which people put on their skin to make themselves smell nice.

words.ex: He asked for permission to leave early.
words.ex_cn: 他请求允许早点离开。
words.en: If someone who has authority over you gives you permission to do something, they say that they will allow you to do it.

words.tr: adj. 似乎合理的；看似真实的；似乎可信的；看似真实的；
words.ex: His excuse sounded plausible.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口听起来似乎合理。
words.en: An explanation or statement that is plausible seems likely to be true or valid.

words.ex: There are plentiful apples in the basket.
words.ex_cn: 篮子里有丰富的苹果。
words.en: If something is plentiful, there is a lot of it available.

words.ex: There is plenty of food for everyone.
words.ex_cn: 每个人都有充足的食物。
words.en: A large or sufficient amount or quantity; more than enough.

words.ex: This portable charger works well on trips.
words.ex_cn: 这个便携式充电器在旅行时很好用。
words.en: Capable of being carried or moved about with ease.

words.ex: He is practically always late for class.
words.ex_cn: 他几乎总是上课迟到。
words.en: In a way that is almost true or almost the case; virtually.

words.ex: The preceding chapter explains the basics.
words.ex_cn: 前一章解释了基础知识。
words.en: Existing or coming before something else in time, order, or importance.

words.ex: The predominant color in the room is blue.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的主导颜色是蓝色。
words.en: If something is predominant, it is more important, noticeable, or powerful than the other things in a situation.

words.ex: It is probable that he will come tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天来的可能性很大。
words.en: If you say that something is probable, you mean that it is likely to be true or likely to happen.

words.ex: His words had a profound effect on her life.
words.ex_cn: 他的话对她的生活产生了深远的影响。
words.en: If you describe something as profound, you mean that it is very great or intense.

words.tr: adj. 正确的；合适的；正当的；
words.ex: This is the proper way to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 这是解决这个问题的正确方法。
words.en: If something is proper, it is suitable or correct for a particular purpose, situation, or person.

words.ex: He puffed after running up the stairs.
words.ex_cn: 他跑上楼梯后喘着气。
words.en: If you puff, you breathe in and out quickly and with force, for example because you have been running or because you are out of breath. A puff of something such as air or smoke is a small amount of it that is blown out from somewhere.

words.tr: adj. 纯的；纯净的；纯粹的；
words.ex: She drank pure water from the spring.
words.ex_cn: 她喝了从泉水中取的纯净水。
words.en: Something that is pure is clean and does not contain any harmful substances.

words.ex: The machine purifies water by removing dirt.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器通过去除杂质来净化水。
words.en: To purify something means to make it clean and pure by removing dirty or harmful substances from it.

words.ex: We need to quantify the results of the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要量化实验的结果。
words.en: If you try to quantify something, you try to calculate how much of it there is.

words.ex: The study uses quantitative data to measure results.
words.ex_cn: 这项研究使用定量数据来测量结果。
words.en: Relating to, measuring, or measured by the quantity of something rather than its quality.

words.ex: The quantity of water in the bottle is small.
words.ex_cn: 瓶子里的水量很少。
words.en: A quantity is an amount that you can measure or count.

words.tr: adj. 古怪的；难以解释的
words.ex: He is queer and proud of who he is.
words.ex_cn: 他是同性恋，并为自己是谁而自豪。
words.en: Queer is used to describe something that is strange or unusual, or someone who is homosexual.

words.ex: The child is quiet during nap time.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在午睡时很安静。
words.en: Making little or no noise; free from disturbance or tumult; tranquil; calm.

words.ex: It is quite cold today.
words.ex_cn: 今天很冷。
words.en: To a certain or fairly significant extent or degree; fairly.

words.tr: adj. 发光的；辐射的；容光焕发的
words.ex: The radiant sun warmed the garden.
words.ex_cn: 明亮的太阳温暖了花园。
words.en: If you describe someone as radiant, you mean that they look very happy and healthy.

words.ex: He rarely eats fast food.
words.ex_cn: 他很少吃快餐。
words.en: Not often; seldom.

words.ex: It is rational to save money for the future.
words.ex_cn: 为未来存钱是合理的。
words.en: Based on or in accordance with reason or logic.

words.tr: adj. 现实的；现实主义的；
words.ex: He made a realistic plan to save money.
words.ex_cn: 他制定了一个现实的存钱计划。
words.en: If you are realistic about a situation, you recognize and accept its true nature and try to deal with it in a practical way.

words.ex: The movie shows a fantasy, not reality.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示的是幻想，而不是现实。
words.en: Reality is the state of things as they actually exist, rather than as they may appear or might be imagined.

words.tr:
n. 后部；
v. 饲养；抚养；
adj. 后面的；
words.ex: The rear of the car was damaged in the accident.
words.ex_cn: 汽车的后部在事故中受损了。
words.en: The back part of something, especially a building or vehicle; to bring up and care for a child until they are fully grown.

words.ex: The extra chair is redundant because we have enough seats.
words.ex_cn: 这把额外的椅子是多余的，因为我们已经有足够的座位了。
words.en: If you are made redundant, your employer tells you to leave because your job is no longer necessary or because there is no more work for you.

words.ex: He is a reliable friend who always helps.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个可靠的朋友，总是帮忙。
words.en: Able to be trusted to do or provide what is needed or right.

words.tr:
v. 喜欢；享受；从…获得乐趣
n. 享受；乐趣；调味品
words.ex: He relishes every bite of his favorite food.
words.ex_cn: 他享受着每一口他最喜欢的食物。
words.en: If you relish something, you enjoy it very much.

words.ex: The remainder of the cake was given to the neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 蛋糕的剩余部分给了邻居。
words.en: The remainder is what is left over after other parts have been taken away or used.

words.tr: adj. 不同寻常的；非凡的；显著的；值得注意的；
words.ex: She made a remarkable improvement in just one month.
words.ex_cn: 她在短短一个月内取得了不同寻常的进步。
words.en: Unusual or striking in a way that attracts attention.

words.ex: The remnant of the old wall still stands.
words.ex_cn: 这堵旧墙的残余部分仍然矗立着。
words.en: A remnant is a small remaining quantity of something.

words.tr:
adj. 偏远的；久远的；
n. 遥控器；
words.ex: The village is in a remote area far from the city.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄位于远离城市的偏远地区。
words.en: Remote areas are far away from cities and places where most people live, and are therefore difficult to get to.

words.tr:
n. 请求；要求的事；
v. 要求；请求；
words.ex: He made a request for help.
words.ex_cn: 他提出了一个帮助的请求。
words.en: If you request something, you ask for it politely or formally.

words.ex: This job requires patience.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作需要耐心。
words.en: If you require something, you need it or want it.

words.tr: n. 需求；要求；必要条件；
words.ex: The job has a requirement of two years of experience.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作的要求是两年经验。
words.en: A requirement is something that is necessary or that must be done.

words.tr:
v. 给…打电话；响铃；
n. 环；环形物；铃声；拳击场；
words.ex: I will ring you tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我明天给你打电话。
words.en: A ring is a small circular band, typically of precious metal and often set with one or more gemstones, worn on a finger as an ornament or a token of marriage, engagement, or authority. It can also refer to the act of making a clear resonant or vibrating sound, or to encircle or surround something.

words.tr:
v. 吼叫；咆哮
n. 吼叫；咆哮
words.ex: The lion let out a loud roar.
words.ex_cn: 狮子发出了一声响亮的咆哮。
words.en: If something roars, it makes a very loud noise, like the sound of a lion.

words.ex: He gave her a romantic gift on Valentine's Day.
words.ex_cn: 他在情人节送了她一份浪漫的礼物。
words.en: If you describe something as romantic, you mean that it is connected with love or with a feeling of excitement and mystery associated with love.

words.tr:
n. 常规；例行公事；
adj. 常规的；例行公事的；
words.ex: He follows a morning routine every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都遵循固定的惯例。
words.en: A routine is a sequence of actions regularly followed; a fixed program.

words.ex: The children are playing in a safe park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在安全的公园里玩耍。
words.en: If something or someone is safe, they are not in danger or likely to be harmed.

words.ex: The fence safeguards the garden from animals.
words.ex_cn: 围栏保护花园免受动物侵扰。
words.en: A safeguard is a measure taken to protect someone or something from potential harm or danger.

words.ex: Wearing a helmet improves your safety.
words.ex_cn: 戴头盔能提高你的安全。
words.en: Safety refers to the condition of being protected from or unlikely to cause danger, risk, or injury.

words.tr:
n. 批准；允许；认可；制裁；处罚
v. 批准；认可；制裁；处罚
words.ex: The company got official sanction to open a new branch.
words.ex_cn: 该公司获得了开设新分公司的正式批准。
words.en: A sanction is a penalty for disobeying a law or rule, or an official permission or approval for an action.

words.tr: n. 香味；香水；气息；察觉；
words.ex: The flower has a sweet scent.
words.ex_cn: 这朵花有甜美的香味。
words.en: A scent is a pleasant smell, especially one that is characteristic of a particular thing. It can also refer to the ability to detect smells or a clue or indication of something.

words.ex: The child screamed when she saw the dog.
words.ex_cn: 当那个孩子看到狗时，她尖叫了起来。
words.en: If you scream, you shout or cry in a loud high-pitched voice, usually because you are in pain or are very frightened.

words.ex: We walked along the seaside at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 我们在日落时沿着海边散步。
words.en: The area by the sea, especially a beach area where people go for holidays.

words.tr:
v. （使）获得；
adj. 安全的；稳定的；
words.ex: He worked hard to secure a job.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以获得一份工作。
words.en: If you secure something that you want or need, you obtain it, often after a lot of effort.

words.tr: n. 安全；保障；防护措施；
words.ex: The school improved security to protect students.
words.ex_cn: 学校加强了安全措施以保护学生。
words.en: Security refers to the state of being free from danger or threat, or measures taken to ensure safety.

words.tr: adj. 敏感的；感情脆弱的；体贴的；善解人意的；
words.ex: He is sensitive to loud noises.
words.ex_cn: 他对大声响很敏感。
words.en: If you are sensitive to other people's needs, problems, or feelings, you understand and are aware of them.

words.tr:
n. 假象；假冒者；冒牌货
adj. 虚假的
v. 假装
words.ex: The gift was a sham, not real.
words.ex_cn: 这份礼物是假的，不是真的。
words.en: A sham is something that is not what it appears to be and is intended to deceive people.

words.tr: adj. 锋利的；骤变的；灵敏的；尖刻的；
words.ex: The knife is sharp enough to cut paper.
words.ex_cn: 这把刀足够锋利，可以切纸。
words.en: Having a thin edge or a fine point that is capable of cutting or piercing; keen.

words.ex: It was sheer luck that he won the game.
words.ex_cn: 他赢了比赛完全是运气。
words.en: Sheer is used to emphasize that a state or situation is complete and does not involve or is not mixed with anything else.

words.ex: The children played on the shore of the lake.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在湖岸玩耍。
words.en: The land along the edge of a sea, lake, or other large body of water.

words.ex: He walked sideways to avoid the puddle.
words.ex_cn: 他斜着走以避开水坑。
words.en: Moving or directed toward one side.

words.tr:
v. 叹息；叹气
n. 叹息；叹气
words.ex: He sighed when he saw the messy room.
words.ex_cn: 他看到凌乱的房间时叹了口气。
words.en: To sigh is to let out a deep breath slowly and audibly, often as a sign of sadness, tiredness, or relief.

words.ex: The significance of this discovery changed science.
words.ex_cn: 这一发现的重要性改变了科学。
words.en: The quality of being worthy of attention; importance.

words.tr: adj. 重大的；重要的；影响明显的；
words.ex: This discovery is a significant step forward.
words.ex_cn: 这一发现是一个重大的进步。
words.en: Something that is significant is important or large enough to be noticed or to have an effect.

words.ex: There was silence after the bad news.
words.ex_cn: 坏消息传来后，一片沉默。
words.en: The absence of sound; complete quiet.

words.ex: The children were silent during the movie.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在看电影时很安静。
words.en: Someone or something that is silent makes no noise at all.

words.ex: He gave a sincere apology.
words.ex_cn: 他真诚地道歉了。
words.en: If you say that someone is sincere, you approve of them because they really mean the things they say.

words.tr: adj. 单一的；单独的；单身的；
words.ex: He bought a single ticket for the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一张单程公交车票。
words.en: Only one in number; one only; not married or not involved in a stable romantic relationship.

words.tr: adj. 单个的；单数的；特异的；
words.ex: Each singular student must submit a form.
words.ex_cn: 每个学生都必须提交一份表格。
words.en: In grammar, singular means relating to or being a form of a word that refers to one person or thing.

words.ex: The siren sounded loudly as the fire truck rushed by.
words.ex_cn: 消防车疾驰而过时，警报器发出了响亮的声音。
words.en: A siren is a device that makes a loud prolonged sound as a signal or warning. It can also refer to a woman who is considered to be alluring or fascinating but also dangerous.

words.ex: The site of the old church is now a park.
words.ex_cn: 旧教堂的位置现在是一个公园。
words.en: A site is a piece of ground that is used for a particular purpose or where a particular thing happens.

words.tr: adj. 位于…的；处于…的境地的； v. 使位于；使坐落于；“situate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The house is situated near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子位于湖边。
words.en: If something is situated in a particular place or position, it is in that place or position.

words.tr: v. 砰地关上；猛地一动；抨击
words.ex: He slammed the door angrily.
words.ex_cn: 他生气地把门砰地关上。
words.en: If you slam a door or window, or if it slams, it shuts noisily and with great force.

words.tr: n. 切片；薄片；部分；片段；
words.ex: She ate a slice of bread for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 她早餐吃了一片面包。
words.en: A slice of something is a thin piece or portion of it.

words.ex: He has a slight cold.
words.ex_cn: 他有点轻微的感冒。
words.en: A slight change, difference, or action is not very great or important.

words.tr:
n. 闻；气味；嗅觉；
v. 嗅；闻；散发气味；察觉；
words.ex: The smell of fresh bread made me hungry.
words.ex_cn: 新鲜面包的香味让我饿了。
words.en: The faculty or power of perceiving odors or scents by means of the organs in the nose.

words.tr:
adj. 平滑的；平坦的；
v. 使平滑；
words.ex: The glass surface is smooth.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃表面是平滑的。
words.en: Having an even and regular surface or consistency; free from projections, indentations, or roughness.

words.tr:
n. 喷嚏；喷嚏声
v. 打喷嚏
words.ex: He had a cold and let out a loud sneeze.
words.ex_cn: 他感冒了，打了一个响亮的喷嚏。
words.en: To sneeze is to suddenly expel air from the nose and mouth due to irritation in the nasal passages.

words.ex: He gave a sniff of the flower.
words.ex_cn: 他闻了闻那朵花。
words.en: To sniff is to breathe in air through your nose in a way that makes a noise, especially when you are trying to smell something or when you have a cold.

words.ex: The price of oil soared last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月石油价格骤升。
words.en: To rise or increase dramatically in amount or level.

words.tr:
v. 呜咽；抽噎
n. 抽噎（声）；啜泣（声）
words.ex: The little girl sobbed after losing her toy.
words.ex_cn: 小女孩在丢失玩具后哭了起来。
words.en: To cry noisily, taking in short breaths.

words.tr: adj. 清醒的；严肃的；素淡的；
words.ex: He stayed sober after drinking only water.
words.ex_cn: 他只喝了水，保持清醒。
words.en: If you are sober, you are not drunk. If you are sober, you are serious and thoughtful.

words.tr:
adj. 唯一的；
n. 鞋底；
words.ex: He is the sole owner of the shop.
words.ex_cn: 他是这家商店唯一的主人。
words.en: If you describe something as the sole thing of a particular kind, you mean that it is the only one of that kind.

words.ex: The ceremony was solemn and quiet.
words.ex_cn: 仪式庄严而安静。
words.en: Solemn means very serious and not cheerful, often because something important or sad is happening or being remembered.

words.tr: adj. 独自的；单独的；孤寂的；
words.ex: He lives in a solitary house far from the town.
words.ex_cn: 他住在离城镇很远的独自一人的房子里。
words.en: A solitary person or thing is the only one in a place.

words.ex: I am somewhat tired after work.
words.ex_cn: 下班后我有点累。
words.en: You use somewhat to indicate that something is the case to a limited extent or degree.

words.ex: I left my keys somewhere in the house.
words.ex_cn: 我把钥匙落在房子的某个地方了。
words.en: In or to some place.

words.ex: The lemon tastes sour.
words.ex_cn: 这个柠檬尝起来是酸的。
words.en: Having a sharp, acidic taste; not sweet.

words.tr:
n. 南方；
adj. 南方的；
adv. 在南方；
words.ex: The sun rises in the east and sets in the south.
words.ex_cn: 太阳从东方升起，在南方落下。
words.en: The south is the direction which is on your right when you are looking towards the direction where the sun rises.

words.ex: He lives in the southern part of the city.
words.ex_cn: 他住在城市的南部。
words.en: Located in or characteristic of a region in the south.

words.ex: The new house has a spacious living room.
words.ex_cn: 这所新房子有一个宽敞的客厅。
words.en: A spacious room, building, or place is large in size or area, so that you can move around freely in it.

words.tr:
v. 抽出；节省；
adj. 备用的；多余的；空闲的；
words.ex: Can you spare a few minutes to help me?
words.ex_cn: 你能抽出几分钟帮我吗？
words.en: If you have something such as time, money, or space to spare, you have some extra time, money, or space that you have not used or which you do not need.

words.tr:
adj. 特别的；特殊的；
n. 特价；特色菜；专车；特别的物品；
words.ex: This is a special day for me.
words.ex_cn: 这一天对我来说很特别。
words.en: Something that is special is different from normal things, or is considered to be better than normal things.

words.ex: Her speciality is cooking Italian food.
words.ex_cn: 她的专长是做意大利菜。
words.en: A speciality is a particular field of work or study that someone specializes in, or a product that is particularly associated with a specific place or producer.

words.ex: This factory specializes in making electric cars.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂专用于制造电动汽车。
words.en: If you specialize in a particular subject or skill, you become an expert in it by focusing your studies or work on it.

words.ex: He specialises in repairing old clocks.
words.ex_cn: 他专用于修理老式钟表。
words.en: To concentrate on and become expert in a particular subject or skill.

words.tr: adj. 特定的；明确的；具体的；
words.ex: He gave a specific reason for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个迟到的具体原因。
words.en: If someone is specific, they give a description that is precise and exact.

words.ex: The sunset was spectacular.
words.ex_cn: 日落非常壮观。
words.en: Something that is spectacular is very impressive or dramatic.

words.ex: The soup is too spicy for me.
words.ex_cn: 这汤对我来说太辣了。
words.en: Food that is spicy has a strong, hot flavor.

words.tr: adj. 壮观的；辉煌的；极好的；
words.ex: The sunset over the mountains was splendid.
words.ex_cn: 山上的日落非常壮观。
words.en: If you say that something is splendid, you mean that it is very good.

words.tr:
n. 地点；场所；斑点；
v. 发现；识别；
words.ex: This is the spot where we met for the first time.
words.ex_cn: 这是我们第一次见面的地方。
words.en: A spot is a particular place or point. It can also refer to a small mark or stain, or a small amount of something. As a verb, it means to see, notice, or recognize someone or something.

words.ex: The car remained static at the red light.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在红灯前静止不动。
words.en: Something that is static does not move or change.

words.tr:
n. 立体声；立体声音响
adj. 立体声的
words.ex: He plays music on the stereo.
words.ex_cn: 他通过立体声收音机播放音乐。
words.en: A stereo is a sound system that uses two or more separate microphones to record sound and two or more loudspeakers to play it back, so that you hear different parts of the sound coming from different directions.

words.tr: n. 中风；划水动作；一击；
words.ex: He had a stroke last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年中风了。
words.en: A stroke is a medical condition in which poor blood flow to the brain results in cell death. It can also refer to an act of hitting or striking someone or something, or a gentle movement of the hand over a surface.

words.tr: adj. 大量的；重大的；实质性的；
words.ex: He made a substantial profit from the sale.
words.ex_cn: 他从这次销售中获得了大量的利润。
words.en: Something that is substantial is large in size, amount, or importance.

words.ex: The difference between the two colors is subtle.
words.ex_cn: 这两种颜色之间的区别很微妙。
words.en: Something that is subtle is not immediately obvious or noticeable, but is rather indirect or understated.

words.ex: One apple will suffice for now.
words.ex_cn: 一个苹果现在就足够了。
words.en: If something suffices, it is enough to achieve a purpose or to fulfill a need.

words.ex: We have sufficient food for the trip.
words.ex_cn: 我们有足够的食物用于这次旅行。
words.en: If something is sufficient for a particular purpose, there is enough of it for the purpose.

words.tr:
v. 适合；相配；
n. 套装；西装；诉讼；
words.ex: This color suits her well.
words.ex_cn: 这个颜色很适合她。
words.en: A suit is a set of clothes made from the same fabric, usually consisting of a jacket and trousers or a skirt. As a verb, to suit means to be appropriate or acceptable for someone or something.

words.ex: This shirt is suitable for the party.
words.ex_cn: 这件衬衫适合这场派对。
words.en: Something that is suitable for a particular person or thing is right or acceptable for them.

words.tr:
n. 金额；总数；
v. 概括；
words.ex: The sum of the bill is fifty dollars.
words.ex_cn: 账单的金额是五十美元。
words.en: A sum is an amount of money, or the total amount of two or more amounts of money added together.

words.ex: The food at this restaurant is superb.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅的食物极佳。
words.en: If something is superb, its quality is very good indeed.

words.ex: The extra words are superfluous.
words.ex_cn: 这些额外的词是多余的。
